title: Boundary-rank obstructions and measurement-assisted recovery in dissipative flat-band preparation
abstract: Number-conserving cooling can fail to prepare an interacting flat-band target when Pauli exclusion blocks its transfer destinations. We study this failure on vertex-edge decorated graphs at one particle per flat orbital. The rank of a cut block of the flat-orbital Gram matrix bounds the number of residual source directions that can remain flat. For sublinear-range cooling with no Hamiltonian term, separated spin domains on periodic decorated hypercubic lattices support exponentially many stationary states with a nonzero bright-particle density. For a chain with fixed finite cooling range, we construct a physical Fock initial state whose overlap with a wrong dark state is independent of system size. This gives fidelity and bright-density bounds valid at every time. In higher dimensions, the bare overlap decays with boundary area, while local boundary rotations prepare states with a finite failure weight in constant circuit depth. Dephasing the occupations of all compact bright modes restores global attraction to the ferromagnetic target when the graph and cooling destinations satisfy the stated conditions. The result allows Hamiltonians that preserve the target. The compressed dynamics in the strong-dephasing limit also remains attractive and has a positive gap at each fixed size. Gram calculations, finite-system dynamics, and Liouvillian spectra test the analytic results. Weak-dephasing and particle-transport bounds constrain the preparation time despite eventual convergence.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the limitations of cooling protocols for preparing interacting flat-band states, showing that Pauli exclusion can cause preparation failure. It quantifies this failure using graph theory (Gram matrix rank) and proves that incorporating measurement-assisted dissipation can restore the system's attraction to the desired ferromagnetic target state.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental obstructions to preparing an interacting flat-band target state using number-conserving cooling protocols in quantum many-body systems.
main_result: It establishes that the rank of a cut block of the flat-orbital Gram matrix provides a quantitative bound on the residual source directions, and that measurement-assisted recovery can restore global attraction to the target state.
method: The analysis employs spectral methods, analyzing the structure of the dark subspace, and deriving bounds using the rank of matrices associated with spatial cuts.
model_or_system: The system is modeled on vertex-edge decorated graphs, studying particle dynamics in a fixed particle sector, often related to flat-band ferromagnetism.
key_observables: Fidelity, bright-particle density, and the rank of the cut block of the flat-orbital Gram matrix.
important_parameters: The cooling range, the graph structure (decorated hypercubic lattices), and the measurement strength ($\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a target state (ferromagnet) and relies on specific conditions for measurement-assisted recovery to guarantee convergence.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometry of the decorated chain, showing the supports of flat/bright orbitals, the blocking mechanism in separated spin domains, and the restoration of attraction via bright-occupation measurements.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the failure mechanism (Pauli exclusion blocking cooling), quantifying this failure using the Gram matrix rank, and then proving recovery mechanisms using measurement-assisted dynamics and dephasing.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium state preparation in correlated systems, which is a major focus area connecting open quantum systems theory with condensed matter physics.
